newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary chemicals hit new highs on good assessment.
newsitem.headline: Hungary chemicals hit new highs on good assessment.

text.p: Both chemicals issues on the Budapest bourse extended recent gains to new all-time highs amid generally good sentiment over the sector, traders said.
Borsodchem opened unchanged at 3,850 forints and rose to a record 3,895 forints. At 1215 GMT Borsodchem stocks stood at 3,870.
"Huge orders have been lodged for Borsodchem stocks in the past few days, mostly from U.S. funds, but also from U.K. funds," said Tibor Papp, salesman at Raiffeisen Securities.
"These orders may have stemmed from the company's roadshow a few months ago, which was linked to a private placement."
Positive corporate news also backed Borsodchem's rise, Papp said, referring to recently published IAS results, expanded capacity and a good PVC price cycle in the last quarter of 1996.

The market's other chemical issue, TVK also rose in even higher volume than Borsodchem in what market participants attributed to a recent analysis by CS First Boston which maintained an earlier "buy" recommendation.
TVK opened at 1,660 forints, up from Friday's close of 1,650 forints and rose to a new record of 1,700. At 1153 GMT TVK shares stood at 1,695.
"The positive recommendation (by CSFB) gave international funds strong confidence," Papp said, adding that domestic investors went along with foreigners in buying the paper.
In a company update on December 11, CS First Boston's analyst Spencer Jakab said TVK share prices were set to rise further on the back of a 2.8 million share buyback by the company.
"Now it seems TVK can easily surpass this 1,700 forint price level by the end of the year," Papp said.
